title: Would a hundred years of new rice reach a lakh?
description: A photo of a seed bank opens the video, and a farmer in Chintamani hears that the country once had about a lakh varieties of rice. One child has tasted only three varieties and wonders about a new one every day for a hundred years. The video stops on that question and shows no answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: a lakh is a very large count, and the days of a lifetime are the thing to compare it with. Ask each child to guess yes or no with a reason, and do not confirm or reject any guess. Watch for students who think a hundred years must be enough because it feels very long.

source: A lakh varieties of rice and {{NAME_1}}'s question
video_script.why: Before any counting, the child meets the real question: how a lifetime of days compares with a lakh.
video_script.substitution: Picture one rice jar for each day of a lifetime, and a lakh jars waiting to be matched.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_1}} tastes one new variety of rice every day for a hundred years: does the count come close to a lakh varieties?
